stem:
Nalini may use the digits 2, 6 and 9 exactly once to make a two-digit number times a one-digit number.

Which claim gives the largest product?

options.text: Any arrangement is largest if it uses a multiplicand; report that label.
Digits may be reused, so try 99 × 6.
Compare the placements systematically: 62 × 9 = 558 is larger than 92 × 6 = 552 and 96 × 2 = 192, so 62 × 9 is largest.
Compare the digit sums of the arrangements instead of the products.

teacher.key_rationale: With digits 2 < 6 < 9 used once, qp × r = 62 × 9 = 558 is largest among the three placements. Naming multiplicand is not a product. Reusing digits drops the once-each condition. Digit sums are outside the product comparison.
